questions.q: Neopentyl bromide, (CH₃)₃C–CH₂Br, is heated in methanol. The main substitution product is:
questions.explain: A 1,2-methyl shift converts the primary cation into a tertiary one, which methanol traps; writing the unrearranged neopentyl ether is the trap.

questions.q: Which halide is LEAST likely to react by the SN1 mechanism?
questions.explain: Aryl cations are very unstable, so aryl halides do not undergo SN1; tertiary and benzylic halides ionise readily.

questions.q: For the hydrolysis of tert-butyl bromide in aqueous acetone, which statement is correct?
options: Rate = k[(CH₃)₃CBr]; ionisation of the C–Br bond is the slow step
The reaction is fastest in a polar aprotic solvent
The carbon is sp³ throughout the reaction
questions.explain: Only the substrate takes part in the slow ionisation, so the reaction is first order; the carbocation intermediate is sp² and planar.

questions.q: Optically active 2-bromobutane undergoes SN1 hydrolysis. The product is best described as:
options: Pure product with retention of configuration
Pure product with inversion of configuration
Largely racemised butan-2-ol, often with slightly more inverted product
questions.explain: The planar cation is attacked from both faces, but the departing halide briefly shields the front face as an ion pair, so racemisation is usually incomplete with inversion slightly favoured.
